headline: Myths About Personal Injury Claims You Should Ignore

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
There's a lot of misinformation swirling around about personal injury claims, and believing the wrong stuff can really mess up your chances of getting fair compensation. Let's bust some common myths:

Myth: You have to accept the first settlement offer from the insurance company.
Fact: Absolutely not! Insurance companies often try to settle quickly and cheaply, especially in car accident cases. Their initial offer is rarely the full value of your claim, and accepting it too soon can leave you without resources if your injuries turn out to be more severe or long-lasting than initially thought.

Myth: If you don't feel pain immediately after an accident, you aren't injured.
Fact: Many serious injuries, like whiplash or even some traumatic brain injuries, can have delayed symptoms. Always seek medical attention after an accident, even if you feel fine. A medical professional can identify issues you might not feel yet.

Myth: You can't afford a personal injury lawyer.
Fact: Most personal injury attorneys, including Angelo J. Reyes, work on a contingency fee basis. This means you don't pay anything upfront, and they only get paid if they win your case. It makes legal help accessible when you need it most.

Myth: Talking to the at-fault driver's insurance company will help your case.
Fact: While you should exchange basic info, giving a recorded statement or discussing your injuries in detail with the other party's insurer without legal guidance can be risky. They're looking for information to minimize their payout. It's best to let an attorney handle these communications.
